Sensor Fusion with Normally Distributed Noise

Given n unbiased sensor measurements of a scalar quantity, each corrupted by independent, normally distributed noise with variance σn2, the likelihood function for the true value (purple, dashed) is also a normal density.

Details

Combining sensor measurements is called sensor fusion. If each sensor measurement is corrupted by independent noise, each measurement provides additional information. The information of a measurement is equal to the inverse of its variance.

The measurements are combined according to Bayes's theorem. Given two measurements z1 and z2 with variances σ12 and σ22, the best estimate for the true value is x̂ = z1 σ22/(σ12 + σ22) + z2 σ12/(σ12 + σ22) with variance σ̂2 = σ12σ22/(σ12 + σ22).

This can be written in recursive form, to update estimate (x̂i, σ̂i2) with measurement (zi, σi2) to form (x̂i+1, σ̂i+12):

Ki = σ̂i2/(σ̂i2 + σ22),
x̂i+1 = x̂i + Ki(z2 − x̂i),
σ̂i+12 = (1 − Ki) σ̂i2.

These recursive equations are the scalar Kalman filter equations, and Ki is also known as the optimal Kalman gain. If only one measurement exists, the combined measurement is identical to the original measurement.
